title: Belgica Antarctic overwintering
summary: The Belgian Antarctic Expedition ship Belgica, under Adrien de Gerlache, became trapped in the pack ice of the Bellingshausen Sea near Peter I Island in late February 1898 and could not leave for about thirteen months. Its crew became the first to endure a full Antarctic winter and its long night; Frederick Cook was the physician and met Roald Amundsen during the voyage. The ship broke free on 14 March 1899.

uncertainty.note: Trapping date: 28 February 1898 (RCE); the Ohio State account says only late February 1898. Release 14 March 1899 in both.

as_recorded.value: the ship became trapped in the ice of the Bellinghausen Sea, near Peter I Island, on February 28th, 1898

Late in February we entered the main body of the sea ice

on March 14, 1899, the Belgian Antarctic Expedition emerged from the pack ice

where.modern_name: Pack ice of the Bellingshausen Sea near Peter I Island, Antarctica (proxy pin at Peter I Island; the ship drifted with the ice)
where.historical_name: Bellingshausen Sea pack ice off Peter I Island (spelled Bellinghausen in the source); Belgian Antarctic Expedition, no sovereign territory

importance.justification: First expedition to winter in the Antarctic region, with Amundsen and Cook among those aboard.
